title: Inhomogeneous cluster DMFT study on p-n junction Mott gap closing in Hubbard lattice
authors: Florian Brette, Eunjae Jeong, Hongchul Choi, Ji Hoon Shim, Geunsik Lee
abstract: Mott gap closing induced by an external potential gradient is studied by considering the Hubbard model on a square lattice. Our model consists of hole- and electron-doped domains forming the p-n junction where the on-site potential varies smoothly across the interface. The effect of the potential drop direction, either along square edge or diagonal, is studied by describing the correlation effects of inhomogeneous 2x2 plaquette impurity clusters within a dynamical mean-field theory framework. It is found that the metallic phase is favored over the Mott insulators when the potential drop becomes comparable to the energy eigenvalue difference of an open 2x2 plaquette between the ground state and the first excited state. Given the same associated electric-field strength, the excitation energy is almost independent of the drop direction, which amounts ~0.35t at U=5.8t with the hopping parameter t. Upon insulator-to-metal transition, the correlated metal exhibits a coherent peak at zero energy whose intensity is greater for the drop direction along the square diagonal than along the edge. The main origin is attributed to the preserved degeneracy of two molecular orbitals for the former case, while it undergoes splitting in the energy levels for the latter. Our result is discussed regarding the experimentally measured Mott gap closing thresholds.
summary: This paper theoretically examines how an external potential gradient across a p-n junction can induce a Mott gap closing in a Hubbard lattice. Using DMFT on plaquette clusters, the authors find that the transition to a correlated metal is governed by the potential drop matching the plaquette's excitation energy. The results highlight the directional dependence of this transition, suggesting that crystal symmetry plays a crucial role in stabilizing the metallic state.
main_problem: The study investigates the Mott gap closing mechanism induced by a spatially varying external potential gradient within a p-n junction formed in a Hubbard lattice.
main_result: The system transitions to a correlated metallic phase when the potential drop strength becomes comparable to the excitation energy of an open 2x2 plaquette, with the diagonal direction exhibiting enhanced coherence.
method: The research employs Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT) coupled with the analysis of inhomogeneous 2x2 plaquette impurity clusters solved via CTQMC simulations.
model_or_system: The model is the Hubbard Hamiltonian on a square lattice, specifically analyzing the physics at a p-n junction where the on-site potential varies smoothly across the interface, characterized by directions [10] and [11].
key_observables: The primary observables include the imaginary part of the central impurity Green's function at zero Matsubara frequency, and the coherent peak intensity in the correlated metal spectrum.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the hopping parameter (t), the on-site repulsion (U), and the external potential drop strength ($\epsilon_{ext}$), with transition thresholds found around $\sim 0.35t$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the inhomogeneous problem onto $2	imes2$ plaquette impurity clusters within the DMFT framework, and comparisons between different potential profiles are made.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the potential profiles along [10] and [11], the calculated impurity Green's functions showing the transition, and energy level diagrams for the $2	imes2$ plaquette showing degeneracy changes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the Hubbard model in a p-n junction, comparing the effects of potential gradients along different lattice directions ([10] vs [11]) using DMFT on plaquette clusters to determine the critical field strength for the insulator-to-metal transition.
why_interesting: The study provides detailed insights into how spatial inhomogeneity (the p-n junction) can tune the Mott insulating state, offering a theoretical framework applicable to engineered correlated materials or interfaces.

figures.caption: Figure 1. The profile of external potential, 𝑉𝑒𝑥𝑡, in the inhomogeneous (inhomo in the figure) region between homogeneous (homo) hole-doped (h-doped) and electron-doped (e-doped) domains. By the periodic boundary condition, one supercell contains two inhomogeneous regions or two junctions. The considered direction across the junction is [10] and [11] in the square lattice.

Figure 2. Indices of inequivalent impurity clusters per one supercell when the external potential is varied along (a) [10], (b) [11]. For [10] or [11] case, there are total 50 or 60 clusters of 2x2 plaquette type, respectively. Owing to the inversion symmetry, the inhomogeneous region between hole-doped and electron-doped regions contains only five independent clusters indexed by I = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 for the former case, while seven (-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3) for the latter case. The potential profile is defined by tanh(x/λ) with x(x10 or x11) = 0 corresponding to the most neutral site.

Figure 3. Plot of 𝑉𝑒𝑥𝑡 values in the left inhomogeneous region in Figure 2 for (a) [10] and (c) [11] cases. Two profiles are plotted for each case, where the steepness is given by the magnitude of dV at the central cluster having x10=0 or x11=0. (b) and (d) are the imaginary part of Matsubara self-energy of the central cluster for the 𝑉𝑒𝑥𝑡 profiles along [10] and [11], respectively.

Figure 4. (a) Profile of 𝑉𝑒𝑥𝑡 for [10]-Asym case, which is similar to Fig. 3(a) but the zero potential level site included. (b) Imaginary part of the central impurity Green’s function at the lowest Matsubara point for chosen values of the field strength (𝜀𝑒𝑥𝑡 ) along [10] and [11] directions. (c) and (d) are the spectra calculated for three selected values of 𝜀𝑒𝑥𝑡, (i)-(iii) for [10]-Asym or (iv)-(vi) for [11] in (b).

Figure 5. (a) Energy levels of four molecular (or single-electron) orbitals and (b) two lowest energy eigenvalues (ground state S=0 and first excited S=1) of four-electron states by exact diagonalization for an isolated 2x2 plaquette against 𝜀𝑒𝑥𝑡 along [10] and [11] directions. (c) Occupation representation of the four-electron ground state |S=0> and first excited state |S=1> for non-zero 𝜀𝑒𝑥𝑡 along [10] and [11] directions. The four horizontal bars indicate the molecular orbital energy levels as plotted in (a). The up and down arrows denote +0.5 and -0.5 values of Sz, respectively.
